The user wants to modify the HTML file to say that this is where Glint Research has been, and that it's time to announce the project but not the model. I need to locate the appropriate place in the HTML to insert that text. So far I've identified the file /home/lane/MythosMini/slm_alliance.html as the relevant page. Using grep I found the "Glint Research" entry around lines 829‑830, inside a featured card within the "Researchers & Engineers" section. The surrounding snippet (lines 815‑870) shows a lot of base64‑encoded image data, which makes the file very large and difficult to read in full. My previous grep commands gave me the exact lines where "Glint Research" appears, but I still need to see the broader context of the <body> section to understand where to place the new announcement text without disrupting existing markup.

The next logical step is to extract a manageable portion of the HTML that includes the body tag and the PEOPLE section, but excludes the massive base64 image lines that blow up the output size. I can achieve this by first filtering out any lines longer than, say, 400 characters (most base64 data lines exceed that length). An `awk 'length($0)<400'` filter will drop those long lines. Then I can pipe the result to `sed` to select the range from the opening `<body>` tag up to the marker `PEOPLE` (which appears in a comment or id near the section I care about). Finally, I’ll limit the output to the first 120 lines to keep it concise for inspection.

Thus, the appropriate command is:
`awk 'length($0)<400' /home/lane/MythosMini/slm_alliance.html | sed -n '/<body/,/PEOPLE/p' | head -120`

This will give me a readable excerpt of the body markup, skipping the bulky base64 image data, and allow me to see where to insert the desired announcement text. I’ll issue this as a Bash tool call.
